result.title: One Schedule Does Not Fit All: Adaptive Inference Schedules for Diffusion Language Models
result.summary: Diffusion language models typically use a fixed denoising schedule across workloads. We show that the cheapest schedule that preserves quality depends on the task, model, and sampler. We propose Task-Calibrated Denoising Allocation (TCDA), a deployment rule with an explicit error guarantee. Given candidate samplers, paired calibration data, a utility tolerance, and guardrails against degeneration, TCDA uses simultaneous one-sided bootstrap bounds to certify which candidates meet both the utility and guardrail criteria. It deploys the cheapest certified candidate or falls back to the full schedule. The probability of deploying an infeasible schedule is asymptotically at most alpha. Candidates include early prefix decoding, state-reusing continuation, reduced time grids, and confidence-threshold decoding. Across seven datasets and two model families, TCDA certifies reductions in denoiser evaluations by factors of 3.4 on XSum and 2.0 on WMT14 for ELF-B; 8.0 on WMT14 and 4.1 on GSM8K for LLaDA-8B; and 1.33 on OpenWebText for both ELF-M and ELF-L. A validation protocol fixed before generation confirmed every selection on fresh seeds. Across 500 calibration splits, false certification remained below 2% in every setting at a nominal level of 5%. Certified schedules vary across tasks and model scales. Trajectory measurements suggest that when decoded tokens commit is more informative for schedule selection than the remaining latent discretization error. We also find that the ELF reference sampler draws its time grid at random, so reproducible schedule comparisons for unconditional generation require fixing the grid.

AI.brief_summary: 论文指出扩散语言模型的最省质量合格去噪调度随任务、模型与采样器而变，提出 TCDA：基于配对校准数据与单侧 bootstrap 同时置信界，认证满足质量与防退化约束的最便宜候选采样方案，否则回退到完整调度。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按任务校准计算量、以统计保证控制误选并保留回退」的框架，可能为 LVR 中 STOP 决策与动态计算分配的成本—收益认证提供线索；但原文限于纯文本扩散模型，未涉及视觉证据筛选或 latent 状态内容。
